answer: Weight grows with the square of tenure, so time locked under one key cannot be compressed or transferred. Each identity locks 20 units in a separate lagoon cell for 8 epochs; weight starts at 1x and reaches its zenith of 9x at epoch 8, and cells cannot merge, so splitting a lock resets tenure to zero. Auditors recompute tenure from checkpoint hashes of each lagoon cell; a history no checkpoint supports is a fable and earns zero weight. Splitting 20 units across 1,000 keys leaves each with a 0.02-unit lock at 1x, while one honest lock matures once and is refunded 2 epochs after exit.
